author: ribeye
dek: Employers added 162,000 jobs in August — nearly triple what economists expected — and one Defiance machine shop still can't fill a single second-shift opening.
disclaimer: Parody: the Schroeder family of Defiance is fictional. The August jobs report is real, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on September 4, 2026.
headline: Jobs Report Blows Past Forecasts, and Defiance Still Can't Fill One Shift

ohio_quotes.quote: I put the sign up in June. I have interviewed eleven people. Nine of them already had jobs, and the other two wanted to know if we had air conditioning, which — fair question, honestly.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Tom Schroeder, Defiance

ohio_quotes.quote: He came home and said, 'Honey, the whole country is hiring.' I said, 'Tom, the whole country has been hiring since 2021. You are not special.'
ohio_quotes.speaker: Karen Schroeder, Defiance

ohio_story: DEFIANCE, Ohio — Tom Schroeder did everything right. He raised the starting wage at his machine shop on the north side of town, he put a "Now Hiring" sign in the window big enough to read from the Maumee River, and he even started offering a $500 bonus to any employee who brought in a friend willing to work second shift. On Friday morning, he learned that the entire American economy had added 162,000 jobs in August. His open position remained, in his words, "as open as it has ever been."

"Food services added 59,000 jobs," Tom said, reading the report on his phone during his lunch break at Cabin Fever Coffee. "Fifty-nine thousand. I can't get one machinist. One. I would take half a machinist at this point. I would take a machinist who only works Tuesdays." The report's other headline numbers offered little comfort: unemployment held steady at 4.1 percent, and July's initially reported loss of 23,000 jobs turned out, on revision, to have been a gain of 21,000. Tom's wife Karen noted that the national economy's rebound had one clear flaw. "Everybody's hiring," she said. "That's the problem. When nobody's hiring, you can hire somebody. When everybody's hiring, you're just another guy with a sign."

The Schroeders are now considering more aggressive measures, including a booth at the Defiance County Fair, a sponsored announcement at the next Defiance High School football game, and — Tom's idea, which Karen has vetoed twice — painting the open position on the side of his truck. "The Buckeyes can't help me, the Browns can't help me," Tom said. "I just need one person who knows what a lathe is and doesn't mind working until eleven. Is that too much to ask in the greatest hiring market in American history? Apparently."
real_summary: The U.S. economy added 162,000 jobs in August 2026, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday, September 4 — nearly triple what economists had expected and well above the average monthly gain of 31,000 over the prior 12 months. The unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1 percent, and the number of unemployed people changed little, at 7.0 million.

Employment grew most in food services and drinking places, which added 59,000 jobs, and in local government education, which added 42,000. Manufacturing added 16,000 jobs and health care added 13,000, while the information industry lost 23,000. Average hourly earnings rose 10 cents to $37.75, up 3.1 percent over the year, and the labor force participation rate edged up to 61.6 percent.

The report also revised the previous two months upward: June's gain was raised by 11,000, from 20,000 to 31,000, and July's initially reported loss of 23,000 jobs was revised to a gain of 21,000, leaving June and July combined 55,000 jobs higher than previously reported.
source_note: BLS Employment Situation release, Sep. 4, 2026: August payrolls +162,000, unemployment 4.1%, sector gains and revisions.
